title: Diabetes Prevention Program (NEJM 2002): study methods
text: The Diabetes Prevention Program randomized 3234 adults without diabetes who had elevated fasting and post-load glucose to placebo, metformin or intensive lifestyle intervention. The trial studied prevention of type 2 diabetes in a high-risk population, rather than treatment of established diabetes. The mean participant age was 51 years and mean BMI was 34.0.

title: Diabetes Prevention Program (NEJM 2002): research results
text: Average follow-up in the Diabetes Prevention Program was 2.8 years. Diabetes incidence was 11.0, 7.8 and 4.8 cases per 100 person-years with placebo, metformin and lifestyle intervention, respectively. Relative to placebo, metformin reduced incidence by 31% (95% CI 17–43%) and lifestyle intervention by 58% (95% CI 48–66%). Lifestyle intervention was more effective than metformin.
